item.text: I’ll make another algorithm-level refactor: add a fast path for values that are already in order, so `insert(...)` only does shifting work when it actually needs to.
The insertion method currently always saves and writes a value, even when the adjacent pair is already ordered. I’m adding a named guard for that no-op case.
The guard is in place. I’m compiling and running the demo to verify the optimized path still produces the same sorted result.
The program still compiles and produces the same output. I’m cleaning up the generated class file and checking the final diff.

Performed another refactor in [insertion_sort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/insertion_sort.java:40).

- Added `isAlreadyOrdered(...)` as a named guard in `insert(...)`.
- Avoids unnecessary shifting/write-back when the adjacent values are already ordered.
